title: Mutabbal (Smoky Aubergine and Tahini with Pomegranate)
summary: Aubergines blackened over a flame until collapsed, drained, chopped by hand and folded into tahini whisked with lemon, garlic and pomegranate molasses, topped with pomegranate seeds, parsley and olive oil.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Char the aubergines
steps.text: Pierce each aubergine a few times. Blacken them directly over a gas flame or a barbecue, turning every few minutes, for 15-20 min, or under a very hot grill for 45-50 min, until the skin is papery and the flesh has completely collapsed.

steps.title: Drain the flesh
steps.text: When cool enough to handle, split them open and spoon the flesh into the colander, leaving the skin behind. Drain for 30 min so the dip is not watery, then chop roughly with a knife.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the tahini with the cold water, lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic and salt until smooth and pale. It may seize at first; keep whisking and it will loosen. Fold in the aubergine and most of the parsley and taste for a balance of smoky, sour and slightly sweet.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spread the mutabbal in the dish, scatter with the pomegranate seeds and remaining parsley and drizzle with olive oil.

tips: A flame gives the smokiest flavour; a few black flecks of skin in the dip are fine.
Serve with warm flatbread, raw vegetables or alongside grilled kofta.
For extra creaminess, stir in 2 tbsp thick yoghurt.
storage: Refrigerate without the topping for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature and add the seeds and oil just before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
